title: Finite constraints and infinite choices: Rado's lemma and distinct representatives

based_on.title: A patching lemma
based_on.venue: Notre Dame Journal of Formal Logic

based_on.title: Hall's marriage theorem
based_on.venue: Journal of the London Mathematical Society (2)

summary: Finite available choices let solutions to every finite selection problem assemble into one global solution.
abstract: Suppose each index has finitely many available choices. Rado's lemma assembles local choices into one global assignment whose values on any finite set of indices occur together in a suitable local assignment. This turns finite solvability into global solvability for constraints preserved by restriction. For choosing distinct values, Hall's theorem gives an exact test: every finite collection of indices must have at least as many available values between them. The test works for arbitrarily many indices when each available set is finite. An infinite available set can make the same finite tests pass while leaving no distinct global choice.
